Project 1: Object Detection on Traffic Light Dataset¶

Maximum Points: 100¶

In this project, the goal is to train an object detection model to detect traffic light color using the dataset provided in this notebook. You can use any framework or model, for example YOLO or RT-DETR and inference techniques like SAHI for better detection of small objects. The focus is on creating an accurate and efficient solution for identifying traffic light color.

The dataset is provided in YOLO format. However, you are free to convert it to any format of your choice according to the library that you are using

The dataset contains a total of 5 classes:

0: 'Green',
1: 'off',
2: 'red',
3: 'wait_on',
4: 'yellow'

Your Tasks¶

  • Train an object detection model.
  • Perform inference on the given video file.
  • Share your inference video in an accessible format, such as uploading it to YouTube or providing a shared drive link.
  • Provide a video or writeup link explaining your code and approach.

Alternatively, you can also upload your writeup document to the online lab.

def yolo_to_xyxy(row, w, h):
    cls, xc, yc, bw, bh = row
    x1 = max(0, int((xc - bw / 2) * w))
    y1 = max(0, int((yc - bh / 2) * h))
    x2 = min(w - 1, int((xc + bw / 2) * w))
    y2 = min(h - 1, int((yc + bh / 2) * h))
    return int(cls), x1, y1, x2, y2

def preview_samples(n=3):
    imgs = [p for ext in ("*.jpg", "*.png") for p in sorted(TRAIN_IMAGES_DIR.glob(ext))]
    if not imgs:
        print("No training images found for preview."); 
        return

    picks = random.sample(imgs, min(n, len(imgs)))
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, len(picks), figsize=(5*len(picks), 5))
    axes = [axes] if len(picks) == 1 else axes

    for ax, img_path in zip(axes, picks):
        img = cv2.cvtColor(cv2.imread(str(img_path)), cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB)
        h, w = img.shape[:2]

        lbl = img_path.parent.parent / "labels" / f"{img_path.stem}.txt"
        if lbl.exists():
            for line in lbl.read_text().splitlines():
                cls, x1, y1, x2, y2 = yolo_to_xyxy([float(x) for x in line.split()], w, h)
                cv2.rectangle(img, (x1, y1), (x2, y2), (0,255,0), 2)
                ax.text(x1, max(12, y1+12), CLASS_NAMES[int(cls)], color="yellow",
                        fontsize=9, bbox=dict(facecolor="black", alpha=0.5, pad=1))

        ax.imshow(img); 
        ax.axis("off")

    plt.tight_layout();
    plt.show()

Project Overview¶

Built and trained a YOLO model to detect five traffic light states: green, red, yellow, off, and wait_on.

Training Configuration¶

Key parameters:

  • Model: yolov8l.pt or yolo11l.pt
  • Epochs: 120
  • Image Size: 960×960
  • Batch Size: 16
  • Device: GPU 0
  • Classes: green, red, yellow, off, wait_on

Training the Model¶

Training was using Ultralytics YOLO:

yolo detect train data=Small Traffic Light.v1i.yolov11/data.yaml model=yolov8l.pt epochs=120 imgsz=960 batch=16 device=0 patience=20

Best model results¶

  • metrics/precision(B) 0.966510
  • metrics/recall(B) 0.745870
  • metrics/mAP50(B) 0.864940
  • metrics/mAP50-95(B) 0.499660

Video Inference¶

The trained weights (best.pt) are used for inference on a test video.

  • https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fi/wi48hs3m1mwv7u787qlhu/inference_traffic_light_video.avi?rlkey=uqyau80jyx889eato6mt69o1q&st=xdkhovj0&dl=0

The trained model achieved strong performance in detecting traffic light colors.
